title: Three-step Embedded SDK Lab Syllabus + Failure Shock Cards
body:
Purpose
This doc is a compact, instructor-friendly syllabus for a three-step hands-on lab that teaches engineers how to embed Redwood SDKs into a small product flow. The goal: move a participant from zero to a minimal production-ready integration in a single half-day session, with explicit probes for common failure modes (the "shock cards") so teams learn recovery patterns.

Audience
- Full-stack and ML engineers new to Redwood SDKs
- Solutions engineers who need replicable onboarding labs for customers
- Developer advocates running workshops and office hours

Learning outcomes (measurable)
1) create a minimal polyglot client that calls Redwood text generation and embeddings with auth, error handling, and streaming
2) configure basic batching and KV cache settings and observe cost/latency tradeoffs in the console
3) detect and recover from three high-impact failure modes (auth expiry, model fallback, network partition) using runtime fallbacks and local stubs

Prerequisites (for participants)
- Laptop with Docker and Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ installed
- GitHub account and basic git fluency
- Access to a Redwood sandbox API key (provisioned via internal form)
- Recommended: basic familiarity with REST/websockets

Session outline (3-step, 3 hours total)
Step 0 — Setup & quick context (20m)- Welcome and goals (3m)- Top-10 quick wins for production serving (7m): batching, prefix caching, pinning, quantization guidance (high level)- Environment provisioning (10m): clone repo, docker up, set API key, run smoke test

Step 1 — Minimal integration + streaming (40m)- Objective: wire a single route that streams generated text to a frontend component- Tasks:
  * Walk through the sample client in repo (node/python) and explain the client lifecycle
  * Implement streaming handler and UI sink (10–15m)
  * Add basic telemetry: request id, latency logging, token counts, model name (10m)
  * Smoke test and share first successful streaming response (5–10m)
- Instructor notes: show console trace and explain token/latency breakdown graph (link to console view).

Step 2 — Embeddings + reranking + cache (50m)- Objective: add an embeddings index for a small FAQ and use client-side reranking to improve relevance- Tasks:
  * Insert sample documents into Redis/SQLite-backed index (template in repo) (10m)
  * Call Redwood embeddings, store vectors, implement nearest-neighbor local search (20m)
  * Add prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt context, show cost delta via mini-metrics (10m)
  * Create a rerank step: candidate generation -> embedding similarity -> final prompt -> generation (10m)
- Instructor notes: point out quality regression checks and how to pin model variants for A/B.

Step 3 — Resilience, cost, and rollout checklist (30m)- Objective: configure resilient routing and run a canary rollout against a fallback model, measure impact- Tasks:
  * Configure a simple routing policy in settings: primary model, fallback smaller model when latency > 300ms or error rate rises (10m)
  * Simulate load/fault: use provided scripts to throttle requests and trigger fallback (10m)
  * Inspect logs/traces and annotate what changed in routing decisions (10m)
- Deliverable: a deployment note (YAML snippet) describing the feature toggle and rollback plan.

Wrap-up & next steps (10m)- Post-lab checklist: secure keys, add observability dashboards, schedule a follow-up code review- Optional homeworks: integrate with language-specific SDK, add automated evals for prompt sets

Instructor materials (what to bring)
- Instructor repo: /labs/embedded-sdk-3-step (branch: workshop-ready)- Slide deck: 10 slides for each step (speaker notes included)- Failure simulation scripts and small dataset

Assessment & gating criteria
- Lab success = participant submits a short PR in the workshop repo with: streaming endpoint, embedding index, and rollout YAML.
- Minimum rubric: auth + error handling implemented, telemetry present, documented rollback plan.

Shock cards (failure learning prompts)
These are short 1-paragraph scenarios the instructor can inject to force trainees to apply recovery patterns. Each card has a quick checklist for the participant.

1) Expiring key mid-demo
Scenario: Your sandbox API key starts returning 401s halfway through Step 2. No one has access to the internal provisioning form.Checklist:
- Switch client to local stub mode (repo has a stub server)
- Attach correlation id to stubbed responses to keep telemetry consistent
- Open a ticket with infra and add a feature flag to hide generation UI
Teaching points: rotate keys without losing telemetry continuity; design your client to tolerate auth errors gracefully.

2) Silent model regression
Scenario: After switching to a new model for better latency, answers drop in quality for the FAQ reranker.Checklist:
- Pin traffic to the previous model variant using routing policy
- Run a quick eval set of 10 prompts and compare embeddings/scores
- Open an eval alert with attached transcripts and repro prompts
Teaching points: always gate model switches behind evals and canary traffic; create small automated prompt suites.

3) Partial network partition to the region (simulates VPC-on-prem hiccup)
Scenario: 30% of requests to the primary region time out with TCP resets.Checklist:
- Trigger automatic fallback to a cross-region pool or smaller local variant
- Temporarily increase retry/backoff window and surface degraded mode in UI
- Log user-facing message and start a mitigation incident playbook
Teaching points: how to reason about SLOs vs degradation; how to communicate degraded experiences to customers.

Quick code sanity checklist (copy for PR template)
- no API keys in repo
- request id and model name logged on every call
- streaming endpoint closes KV cache on error
- fallbacks covered by unit tests (mocked client)

Telemetry probes to enable in the lab
- per-request token_count, latency_ms, model_used, route_decision
- counter for fallback_activated and cache_hit_ratio
- a small trace span around embedding ingestion and rerank flow

Handoff template (to customer/internal eng)
- short README: what changed, how to repro, feature flags used
- rollout YAML with canary percentage and metric thresholds
- list of alerts to enable and recommended dashboards

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want to provide a managed Redis instance for labs or keep local only? (ops cost)
- Should the sandbox API key auto-rotate on long-running workshops to teach rotation?
- Add a pre-recorded video for Step 2 to speed workshops that run with limited instructor bandwidth.

Notes to self (instructor hacks)
- If participants get stuck on embeddings, drop to a prepared code diff that wires the nearest neighbor search (5–7m hack).
- Use shock card 1 at ~minute 75 to reinforce error handling principles.

Appendix: small YAML snippets (examples)
- rollout policy example: |
  primary_model: open-7b-v1
  fallback_model: open-3b-quant
  triggers:
    latency_ms: 300
    error_rate: 0.02

- telemetry tags to include on logs: request_id, workshop_id, participant_handle

Contact and feedback
- Lead instructor: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)
- Workshop feedback form: internal link (collects 10-min retros)
- If this lab gets repeated more than 3 times in a month, propose a lightweight CI harness to auto-reset environments.

----
This draft intentionally mixes syllabus + gamebook style shock cards to increase retention. Use this as a base for a more formal slide deck and a one-page cheat sheet for customers.
